scenarios.label: As-is · direct AD CS
scenarios.summary: The endpoint receives policy from the domain, enrolls directly with AD CS, then presents the resulting machine certificate to 802.1X. Network intent has to be reconstructed from directory structure, names or external mappings.

events.title: Computer identity resolved
events.detail: The machine account exists and its group memberships define which certificate policy may apply.

events.title: Computer policy checked in
events.detail: The endpoint processed computer policy and discovered the enterprise enrollment policy.

events.title: Native enrollment submitted
events.detail: Windows generated a nonexportable key and submitted a PKCS#10 request directly to the enterprise CA.

events.title: Template policy accepted
events.detail: AD CS authorized the requester against the certificate template and issued one certificate.

events.title: Machine certificate installed
events.detail: The issued certificate is linked to the locally generated nonexportable private key.

events.title: 802.1X authentication started
events.detail: The access point relayed the endpoint EAPOL exchange to RADIUS.

events.title: Certificate valid; intent still external
events.detail: The certificate proves machine identity, but its standard fields do not carry stable business intent. RADIUS must consult names, groups or another mapping.

events.title: Access-Accept returned
events.detail: The external mapping selected the engineering network policy.

events.title: Endpoint admitted to VLAN 300
events.detail: The controller applied the RADIUS result and the endpoint joined the assigned network.

scenarios.label: To-be · broker + facts
scenarios.summary: The broker authenticates the same endpoint, resolves authoritative facts, controls certificate claims and records the transaction. RADIUS evaluates stable signed claims without depending on a live directory or CMDB lookup during authentication.

events.title: Computer identity authenticated
events.detail: The broker binds the mutual Kerberos identity to the current directory computer object.

events.title: One controlled policy returned
events.detail: Windows receives a native enrollment policy whose subject and SAN values remain broker-authoritative.

events.title: Authoritative facts queried
events.detail: The broker sends immutable device identity to the configured source-of-truth connector and validates the bounded response.

events.title: Stable intent resolved
events.detail: The response maps typed source data into the approved certificate fact vocabulary.

events.title: CSR and key possession validated
events.detail: The broker validates the native request, binds its SPKI to the authenticated device and constructs the authoritative subject and SAN set.

events.title: Restricted CA request signed
events.detail: The networkless signer authorizes only the bounded request shape required by the restricted AD CS template.

events.title: Broker-controlled certificate issued
events.detail: AD CS issued one certificate using the restricted broker template.

events.title: Certificate installed with signed facts
events.detail: Windows retains its nonexportable key; the certificate now carries the broker-approved fact URI SANs.

events.title: Signed use-case claim accepted
events.detail: RADIUS validates the chain and revocation state, then maps the signed use-case claim directly to local policy.

events.title: Access-Accept returned
events.detail: The locally governed claim mapping selected the engineering network.

events.title: Endpoint admitted to VLAN 300
events.detail: The same network result is reached without a live identity-system lookup in the authentication path.
